Q: The reason for the appearance of dark edges that are at sharp angles A:

Dark edges at sharp angles usually appear because of shadowing or light falloff. When light hits a surface, corners or sharp angles receive less light than flat areas, creating a darker appearance. In imaging or graphics, this is also called vignetting or edge shading, often caused by lens effects or rendering artifacts.

Q: BASH Xprintidle & Firefox A:

Start/stop process regarding desktop idle time

Consider this as a subprocess manager:

#!/bin/bash

url="https://thesite.com/"
browserCmd=(firefox)
browserCmd+=(--kiosk --start-fullscreen --noerrdialogs)
browserCmd+=(--no-first-run --disable-infobars)
browserCmd+=("$url")

while :;do
    if (( $(xprintidle) > 120000 )); then
        if (( browserPid )); then
            kill $browserPid
            browserPid=
        fi
    else
        if ! (( browserPid )); then
            "${browserCmd[@]}" &
            browserPid=$!
        fi
    fi
    sleep .5
done

Q: URL to specific time in video file A:

At the end you add #t=<minutes>:<seconds> or #t=<seconds>

So it would look like this, example for 9 minutes and 12 seconds: https://download.blender.org/peach/bigbuckbunny_movies/BigBuckBunny_320x180.mp4#t=09:12
